subject: [PATCH v2] mm/mempolicy: recompute automatic interleave weights on memory hotplug

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the condition in wi_state_refresh() function does not correctly handle cases where old_wi_state is NULL and mode_auto is true, potentially leading to incorrect behavior.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Gregory,

I think you may have dropped my review tag from the previous
version!!! I believe the only thing that changes is the warn, so
please feel free to add:
Reviewed-by: Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com>

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton noted that the original patch description mentioned that HMAT and CXL report a node's bandwidth only when it first gains memory, but this logic was not correctly applied in the code changes. Specifically, the wi_state_refresh() function should recompute weights whenever N_MEMORY changes, which is already handled by the hotplug notifier. However, the comment also suggests that the original patch description and the code changes are inconsistent, as the original description implies that the weights should be recomputed on every memory hotplug event.
sentiment_signals: inconsistency between patch description and code

2026-10-30.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance regression caused by outdated automatic interleave weights in the Linux kernel's memory policy module (mm/mempolicy). When nodes gain or lose memory, their weights are not recalculated from their reported bandwidths, leading to an uneven distribution of data and potential overload. The patch introduces a new function, wi_state_refresh(), which recomputes the weights based on the recorded bandwidth whenever a node gains or loses its first/last memory. If allocating new weights fails, it warns once and continues with the next recompute starting from the full bandwidth table.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary: Reviewer Joshua Hahn noted that the condition for not recomputing weights from node_bw_table is incorrect, specifically when old_wi_state->mode_auto is false, and suggested no change to his review tag.
sentiment_signals: reviewer's comment indicates no strong objection or disagreement
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Andrew,
Ah, thank you for the catch. Looking through the code again, I think
it still looks good to me so my review tag should stil stay. I'll be
more careful about stuff like this in the future!
